title: fix: reset Whitenoise lifecycle after deleting data
body:
## Description

Fixes the reset lifecycle after deleting all app data.

The bridge now replaces the process-global Whitenoise handle safely: it waits for in-flight bridge calls before closing the old database, clears the global instance after delete, and exposes `reinitializeWhitenoise()` so Flutter can install a fresh instance after the local wipe completes.

Flutter wraps the delete flow with a reset-pending marker. If the app is killed or interrupted during reset, startup recovery clears the local reset surface before initializing Whitenoise again. If deletion succeeds but reinitialization fails in the same process, the app routes to the fatal error flow instead of leaving the user on settings with an uninitialized Rust singleton.

This PR also keeps the start-DM stale-group guard: cached DM group IDs are validated before opening. If the cached group no longer exists in Rust/MDK state, the app falls back to creating a fresh DM instead of failing with `Group not found`.

This app-side lifecycle fix depends on the companion `whitenoise-rs` bounded-delete PR, which prevents local data deletion from hanging behind stuck scheduler/background/relay shutdown work:

https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/840

Closes #660

title: Delete all app data leaves Whitenoise singleton using a closed database pool
body:
## Summary

After using Privacy & security -> Delete App Data, signing in again in the same app process can fail with:

```text
ApiError.whitenoise(message: Database error: SQLx error: attempted to acquire a connection on a closed pool)
```

This appears to happen because the Flutter app deletes all data via the existing Rust `Whitenoise` instance, but the app process keeps the same global Rust singleton alive afterward.

## Evidence

Current app flow:

- `PrivacySecurityScreen` calls `useDeleteAllData()` and passes `deleteAllData` to the destructive confirmation action.
- On success, the screen only resets Flutter auth state and routes home.
- Rust bridge `delete_all_data()` gets the existing `GLOBAL_WN` instance via `wn()?` and calls `whitenoise.delete_all_data()`.
- The app wrapper initializes `GLOBAL_WN` with `OnceCell::get_or_try_init`, so the retained instance cannot be replaced in the same process.
- Upstream `whitenoise.delete_all_data()` calls `shutdown()`, deactivates inbox/relay control, then calls `self.shared.database.close_and_delete_files().await`.
- `close_and_delete_files()` closes the SQLx pool before deleting DB files.
- Subsequent login goes through `login_start`, which uses `self.shared.database`; on the retained instance that database pool is already closed.
- Upstream already has a test comment noting: after `delete_all_data` the database pool is closed, so a fresh `Whitenoise` instance is required for subsequent logins.

## Repro

1. Run the app in the iOS simulator.
2. Sign in or create an account.
3. Go to Privacy & security.
4. Tap Delete App Data and confirm.
5. Without killing/restarting the app process, try to sign in again.

Expected: sign-in works against a freshly initialized empty local store.

Actual: sign-in can fail with `SQLx error: attempted to acquire a connection on a closed pool`.

## Likely fix direction

The app needs an explicit post-delete lifecycle step. Possible approaches:

- Reinitialize Rust after delete by replacing the app wrapper singleton with a fresh `Whitenoise` instance.
- Expose a bridge function that performs delete-all-data and reinitialization atomically from the app config.
- Force a full app-process restart or show a restart-required state after delete, if live reinitialization is not safe yet.

The important invariant is that after full data deletion, no subsequent API call should use the old `Whitenoise` instance whose SQLx pool was closed.

## Idea

Support Markdown rendering in two places:

1. **Inline messages** - Render Markdown formatting (bold, italic, code blocks, links, lists) directly in chat messages.
2. **Uploaded .md files** - When a `.md` file is shared in a group, render a preview of its contents instead of showing it as a raw file download.

This would make group conversations more readable and useful for sharing structured content, documentation, and notes.

title: Add markdown rendering for chat messages
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/35d671f7406873029a2b8cd5e12660eb6642cb3cdbe841a429ae0e94f0d43bff.png)


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/813ae5ee-daef-4bdf-aec6-cd0f390a2198



> Heads up: most of the diff is FRB codegen. Net total is ~7800 added lines; ~4300 of that is autogenerated `lib/src/rust/` and `rust/src/frb_generated.rs`, regenerated whenever the bridge surface changes. The hand-written review surface is ~1500 lines plus ~1700 lines of tests. Skim the codegen, read the rest.

This PR consumes the new `whitenoise_markdown::Document` AST from whitenoise-rs (pinned at `f421a8ad`). Chat bubbles now render CommonMark, GFM, and the nostr-extension format. Plain-text messages render byte-identically to before.

The marmots have learned to read bold text.

## What's in here

- `WnMarkdownText` walks the parsed AST and renders every Block and Inline variant.
- Plain-text fast path: single-paragraph messages with only Text/SoftBreak/HardBreak inlines skip the markdown renderer entirely. They keep the existing inline-timestamp layout.
- `@npub` mentions render as underlined `@DisplayName` (Vlad's design call). Tap opens a new in-app `UserProfileShade` instead of bouncing out to the OS. Non-npub Nostr URIs (note, nevent, nprofile, naddr, nrelay) still route externally because they point at events, not people.
- `SoftBreak` renders as a newline. The CommonMark default is a space, which loses every Enter press in the composer.
- URL scheme allow-list: `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `nostr`, `tel`. Anything else gets no tap recognizer at the renderer layer; the bubble's tap handler reapplies the same check before `launchUrl`. The Rust parser does not recognize HTML, so `<script>` and similar pass through as literal text.
- Surface boundaries: chat-list previews, reply quotes, notifications, and the composer keep their existing plain-text rendering.

## Bridge style

The bridge mirrors each AST type through FRB. The AST is FRB-friendly: owned `String`, `Vec<Enum>` recursion, `Clone`, `Eq`. Generated Dart sealed classes give exhaustive switch and IDE help. A hand-rolled Dart JSON parser would be a second markdown implementation and would drift from upstream.

## Tests + manual QA

- 4498 Flutter tests + 75 Rust tests pass. Coverage 99.03%. `just precommit` clean.
- Manual checklist run locally: every Block and Inline variant, surface boundaries, security cases (`javascript:`, `data:`, raw HTML stay inert), nested containers, CJK and RTL mixed runs, mention-tap into shade and back without scroll jump, long-press preview shows resolved names.

## Known limitations

1. Cross-inline highlight matches are not highlighted in search results.
2. Math renders as italic monospace source; no LaTeX engine is used.
3. Inline markdown images render as `[image: alt]` text links, not embedded.
4. Mentions of users outside the chat's metadata cache fall back to truncated npub until metadata loads. Follow-up could subscribe to mentioned pubkeys.

## Incidental upstream commits

The rev bump pulled in two non-markdown commits: `917ad14` (handle_contact_list lock contention) and `585d31f` (MDK update + push-token gossip). Both required adding `disappearing_message_secs: None` to two struct literals in `rust/src/api/groups.rs`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Rich Markdown rendering for messages (formatted text, headings, code, lists, tables, math)
  * In-chat mention suggestions with resolved display names and insertion support
  * Tappable links and Nostr mentions with safe handling and in-app navigation (including opening profiles/chats)

* **UX Improvements**
  * Quoted-message previews render Markdown when available
  * Start-chat can open as a non-opaque “shade” for smoother flows

* **Localization**
  * Added localized text for unsupported deep-link dialogs (multiple languages)

title: User tag navigation
body:
# Context
When clicking in a user tag in a message bubble, it shows the start chat screen. This is a bit unexpected comparing with other chat apps (like whatsapp or signal) where tags navigate to the same screen that you woudl see when clicking on a group member from the members lists screen.The reason for doing this is that tags in messages may tag users that are not in the group. 

# Solution
A solution that we discussed here https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/pull/665#discussion_r3261928955 would be to keep the start chat navigation only for users that are not members of the group and for group members navigate to the group member screen

⚠️ We don't want to fetch group members in every chat bubble

title: Editable group messages

labels.name: Idea 💡
labels.description: Ideas of changes so we don't forget to re evaluate later

body:
# Context

In the white noise house we wanted to have a shared shopping list. We thought it would be cool to have a way to make some group messages editable, so that anyone can edit. Admins also is also an interesting feature that we could have.
